_about: Attractions within walking distance of DC's Chinatown, used by guides.json. Walk times are Manhattan distance on the street grid at 3 mph, from the Friendship Archway (7th and H) and from the Convention Center's south side (801 Mount Vernon Pl NW). Hours and programs checked Nov 26, 2026; re-check before publishing.

attractions.name: Friendship Archway
attractions.summary: Chinatown's front door since 1986: seven pagoda-style roofs, some 7,000 glazed tiles and 272 painted dragons, paid for jointly by Washington and Beijing.

attractions.name: Capital One Arena
attractions.hours: Event days; check the event listing
attractions.summary: Home ice and home court for the Capitals and Wizards, and the city's biggest indoor concert room. It reopened for the 2026–27 season mid-renovation; much of the $1 billion-plus overhaul is still about a year away.

attractions.name: National Portrait Gallery and Smithsonian American Art Museum
attractions.summary: Two Smithsonian museums share one Greek Revival block: presidents, poets and provocateurs on one side, American art on the other. Enter from F Street or G Street.

attractions.name: Shakespeare Theatre Company: Harman Hall
attractions.summary: The company's larger house, across F Street from the arena.
attractions.current: A Midsummer Night's Dream, directed by Simon Godwin, with puppets by Basil Twist, Dec 4, 2026–Jan 10, 2027.

attractions.name: Shakespeare Theatre Company: Klein Theatre
attractions.summary: The company's original, more intimate house, three blocks south on 7th Street.
attractions.current: A Raisin in the Sun (Lorraine Hansberry; directed by Tim Bond), extended, Jan 23–Mar 7, 2027. Then Romeo and Juliet, Apr 13–May 16, 2027.

attractions.name: Woolly Mammoth Theatre Company
attractions.summary: New plays, often loud and seldom polite, in a modern house off 7th Street.

attractions.name: Ford's Theatre National Historic Site
attractions.hours: Daily; timed entries every half hour, 9 a.m.–4 p.m.
attractions.cost: No entrance fee; timed ticket required (free same-day at the box office, or reserve online for a small fee)
attractions.summary: Where Lincoln was shot, with the museum below and the Petersen House, where he died, across the street. The theater itself may be closed some hours for rehearsals and performances.

attractions.name: National Building Museum
attractions.summary: The Great Hall of the old Pension Building is the draw: one of the largest indoor rooms in the city, ringed by colossal columns.

attractions.name: Capital Jewish Museum
attractions.hours: Check the museum's site; advance reservations recommended
attractions.cost: Free, suggested donation; visitors 18 and older need government ID
attractions.summary: Built around the restored sanctuary of DC's oldest synagogue building, with exhibitions on Jewish Washington.
attractions.current: Special exhibition: Esther Bubley, Photographing the Homefront.

attractions.name: Sixth & I
attractions.summary: A historic synagogue that books author talks, comedy and concerts, a block from the Archway.

attractions.name: National Archives Museum
attractions.summary: The Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights, a straight walk down 7th Street.

attractions.name: DowntownDC Holiday Market
attractions.address: F St NW between 7th and 9th Streets
attractions.summary: More than 115 vendors on the street outside the Portrait Gallery, including stalls from Lucky Danger and Daikaya.

attractions.name: Walter E. Washington Convention Center
attractions.summary: The reason many readers of this guide are in the neighborhood. Every walk time in the guide is measured from its south side on Mount Vernon Square.
